But we need to assign each module to exactly one component. Could group top-level __init__ with others? Might be its own component but we want small number. - bookshop.api (package) - no imports, no classes/functions. Could be part of API component.

- bookshop.application (package) - no imports.

- bookshop.application.checkout - Use-case service for checkout. Imports domain.pricing, domain.order, infrastructure.order_repository, infrastructure.payment_gateway.

- bookshop.application.inventory - Use-case service for browsing/searching stock. Imports domain.book, domain? Actually imports domain.book and infrastructure.book_repository.

- bookshop.domain (package) - no imports.

- bookshop.domain.order - Order aggregate. Imports dataclasses, enum, domain.book.

- bookshop.domain.pricing - Pure pricing rules. Imports domain.order.

- bookshop.infrastructure (package) - no imports.

- bookshop.infrastructure.book_repository - In-memory persistence adapter for book catalog. Imports domain.book, domain.catalog.

- bookshop.infrastructure.order_repository - In-memory persistence adapter for orders. Imports domain.order.

- bookshop.infrastructure.payment_gateway - Adapter to external payment provider. No imports.

Thus we can think of layers: API (presentation), Application (use cases), Domain (model), Infrastructure (persistence/adapters). This is typical layered architecture.

3. Domain: modules: bookshop.domain, bookshop.domain.book, bookshop.domain.catalog, bookshop.domain.order, bookshop.domain.pricing

4. Infrastructure: modules: bookshop.infrastructure, bookshop.infrastructure.book_repository, bookshop.infrastructure.order_repository, bookshop.infrastructure.payment_gateway
